newsitem.title: USA: Publix supermarkets to pay $81.5 million in gender case.
newsitem.headline: Publix supermarkets to pay $81.5 million in gender case.

text.p: Publix Super Markets Inc. has agreed to pay $81.5 million to settle a class action case that said it discriminated against female employees, lawyers for the plaintiffs said on Friday.
The suit alleged Publix discriminated against women in job assignments, promotions, allocation of working hours, and limited their advancement, pay and employment opportunities.
Filed in July 1995, it involved more than 150,000 women currently or previously working in its chain of grocery stores.

"We brought this lawsuit because we care about Publix and wanted to make it a better company. We are pleased to have been involved in a process that will help ensure a level playing field for all employees," plaintiff Janet McClung said in a statement issued by the lawyers.
Publix is the largest private employer in Florida and operates 533 retail grocery stores in Florida, Georgia, South Carolina and Alabama. About half its 100,000-strong workforce is female.
The lawyers' statement said Publix agreed to pay $81.5 million to settle the suit with payments expected to be made within a year.

Publix also undertook to set up a system by which employees could register their interest in moving to management or other jobs, to develop training for managers and supervisors in equal opportunities, and to establish a complaints procedure for gender discrimination.

"This case was able to be resolved because Publix acted responsibly by demonstrating a willingness to take hard look at its employment practices and make improvements to ensure equal opportunites for its female employees in the retail stores," the plaintiffs' lead counsel, Barry Goldstein, said.
"The changes Publix agreed to will make it an even better place to work."
